title: Tillman's 26 seal Sabah's fourth straight ABL crown
description: Sabah completed a clean sweep of the Azerbaijan Basketball League finals on Monday, blitzing Absheron Lions 108-95 in Game 3 at Baku Sports Hall to claim their fourth consecutive championship under legendary Lithuanian coach Rimas Kurtinaitis. American center Justin Tillman (203-F-1996, college: VCU) was named Finals MVP immediately after the clincher, capping a dominant series with 26 points on 11-of-16 from the field, eight rebounds, and two blocks. The 26-year-old attacked the rim relentlessly, converting at nearly 69 percent from two-point range as Absheron's interior defense had no answer. Hassani Gravett (188-G-1996, college: S.Carolina) orchestrated the victory with 24 points (7-of-15 from two, 3-of-6 from three), nine assists, and seven rebounds in 32 minutes, while Keith Jordan (198-SF-1998, college: SHU) added 14 points on a perfect 5-of-5 from inside the arc. title: Sabah clinch third straight D1 title
description: Neftci - Sabah 78-83 Sabah celebrated D1 title. They outscored Neftci in Game 6 of the championship series to lift the trophy. The best player for the winners was Latvian center Klavs Cavars (208-1996) who had a double-double by scoring 21 points and 11 rebounds (on 9-of-10 shooting from the field). American guard Hassani Gravett (188-1996, college: S.Carolina) chipped in 21 points, 7 rebounds and 5 assists. At the other side the best for losing team was international point guard Kamran Mammadov (187-2000) who recorded 17 points and 6 assists and American center Marvin Jefferson (206-1986, college: Idaho, agency: BIG) added 18 points, 6 rebounds and 5 blocks respectively. Both teams had four players each who scored in double figures.
imageCaption: Sabah clinch third straight D1 title (Photo: aze.basketball)

title: Sabah crowned ABL champions
description: Xezri - Sabah 69-74 Sabah claimed their second ABL title. They overcame Xezri on the road in Game 4 to lift the trophy. Worth to mention a great performance of American guard Desmond Cambridge Jr (193-1998, college: Arizona St.) who helped to win the game recording 15 points, 7 rebounds and 5 assists. The international swingman Shirzad Shirzadov (188-2000) contributed with 18 points and 6 rebounds for the winners. He was named the MVP. American guard Jordan Perkins (185-1998, college: Longwood) replied with a double-double by scoring 16 points and 12 assists and the former international power forward Amil Hamzayev (203-1990) added 15 points and 14 rebounds in the effort for Xezri. Four Xezri players scored in double figures.

title: ABL Round 5 of Finals. Sabah nip Gence to claim the title
description: Sabah - Gence 86-85 Sabah are ABL 22/23 champions. They narrowly defeated Gence in the decisive fifth game of the championship series to conquer the trophy. Great defensive blocking was one of the keys in this match when Sabah made 10 blocks. Canadian center Christian Rohlehr (209-1997, college: SFC) saved the victory with a double-double by scoring 25 points and 12 rebounds. American forward AJ Patty (204-1995, college: MSU) contributed with a double-double by scoring 22 points and 13 rebounds for the winners. American guard Collin Turner (185-1995, college: Angelo St.) answered with a triple-double by scoring 26 points, 10 rebounds, 11 assists and 5 steals and the other American import forward Jordan Madrid-Andrews (203-1994, college: Richmond) added 20 points and 11 rebounds in the effort for Gence. Four Gence players scored in double figures.
imageCaption: Sabah nip Gence to claim the title (Photo: aze.basketball)

title: Zirve announced champions, the season is over
description: Zirve have been announced champions of 2019/20 season as it have been cut short in the light of coronavirus safety risks. The team finished on top with an 18-2 record. All the games are canceled and no play-offs this year. The foreigners of the teams are now on their way back home.
